newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish mkts hold breath ahead of next week's data.
newsitem.headline: Polish mkts hold breath ahead of next week's data.

text.p: Poland's financial markets, split on whether the central bank will raise official interest rates after recently hiking up market rates, are likely to get some direction from key end-of-year data releases next week.

The Central Statistical Office (GUS) is due to release last month's CPI data on Wednesday, January 15, and the National Bank of Poland will most likely release December's money supply figures, according to a senior banking source.
GUS is also sheduled to release December's producer prices and industrial output on Friday, January 17.

"Players are nervously awaiting next week's data, which could signal if the central bank will change rates cosmetically or leave them alone for now," said Radoslaw Radziszewski, deputy chief dealer at Pekao SA.

Analysts expected year-on-year inflation to fall to around 18.8 percent in December while the Finance Ministry and the central bank said price growth would fall to about 18.5 percent last year, from 21.6 percent in 1995.

"If December's inflation is above market expectations and credit action countinues to grow quickly, it would put pressure on the central bank to up rates, even symbolically," said Bartlomiej Kumela, senior dealer at Societe Generale.

Analysts said that despite a division in market views about the possibility of an official rate rise, yields would rise at next Monday's one billion zloty primary T-bill auction after the central bank lifted the lid off NBP-bill yields.
Over the last four weeks the central bank let NBP-bill yields rise by more than two percentage points to 22 percent, simultaneously pulling up deposit rates.

Analysts said Monday's T-bill tender was likely to be undersubscribed again as banks were more keen on investing in higher yielding NBP-bills and waiting for the central bank's interest rate intentions to clarify.

They said average yields of the benchmark 52-week T-bill were likely to rise to just below 20.0 percent on Monday from 19.84 at the last primary auction, while 13- and 26-week bills would rise to around 19.7 from 18.99 and 19.37 respectively.
"Foreign interest in Polish paper is slowly starting to return as yields rise, but big clients have yet to reappear," one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw said.

Analysts said many foreign investors were holding off with Polish T-bill or bond purchases because of the zloty's expected weakening against its basket of five currencies later this year on the back of unfavourable fundamentals.
But analysts said the zloty could get a temporary boost if the central bank increased official rates, before the expected huge trade deficit would slowly pull the currency down.

"If rates rise the zloty could see above 3.2 percent from the parity rate, but any longer term gains would likely be offset by the negative trade balance," said Pawel Lopuszynski, senior forex dealer at Pekao SA.
The zloty finished the week at 2.8950 to the dollar and at 1.8360 against the mark, or about 3.13 percent from the centre of the currency's 14-percent daily trading band.
